task.name: Mid-run re-exec re-enters sprint startup, re-running pre-work checks against a live sprint
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A mid-run re-exec re-enters full sprint startup, including the steps that are
only meaningful before any work has begun. Those steps then run against a
machine that is busy executing the sprint's own stories, and against state the
new process does not recognise as its own. Two sprints have been killed this way
in two days, by different startup steps.

Sprint `a865b3e0fe03` (2026-07-27) was running two stories when a story pulled
new source and triggered a re-exec:

```
08:37:43 [issue-1992] Source updated after pull — re-execing to load new code
         Detached sprint starting
         WARNING: skipping issue #1979 — issue #1979 is already closed
         DROPPED issue-1945: active worktree collision after re-exec; continuing with remaining stories.
         ⚠ WORKSPACE  stale worktree detected — removing feat/issue-1945
08:38:11 Running gate: make gate
08:40:13 Broken baseline: configured gate failed on sprint merge base
         9b09d56... before any dev work started (Gate timed out after 120s)
```

Three separate startup behaviors fired against a live sprint. A running story
was dropped as a worktree collision with itself and its worktree removed. The
baseline gate — whose stated purpose is to establish that the merge base is
green *before any dev work started* — ran while agents were consuming the host,
and timed out at 120s on a suite that completes in roughly 30s idle. The sprint
then raised and died.

The same startup sequence had killed the previous evening's sprint through a
different step: that time the baseline gate failed on a configuration rule a
story had merged minutes earlier.

The condition is self-triggering under dogfooding. A sprint merges its own
stories, the base branch advances, the next workspace pull observes new source,
and the re-exec follows.

## Diagnosis

**Observed symptom:** a healthy sprint terminated at a startup check that has no
meaning mid-run, having first discarded a running story.

**Evidence — the contention was predicted at launch.** The sprint emitted, in
its own startup output:

```
gate_timeout: baseline=60s mode=adaptive parallel=2 gate_cpu_cores=10 host_cores=10 demand=20 factor=2.00 effective=120s
WARNING: gate CPU demand (10 cores × parallel 2 = 20 cores) exceeds host capacity (10 cores)
  by >50%; consider lowering --parallel to avoid contention-driven gate timeouts
```

The effective timeout is derived on the assumption that the gate contends only
with the sprint's configured parallelism. When the same check re-runs mid-flight,
it additionally contends with the agents already in progress, which the
derivation does not model.

**Evidence — the re-exec does not recognise its own stories.** The new process
classified `issue-1945` as an active-worktree collision and dropped it, then
treated its worktree as stale, while the story's own agent process group was
still alive; it was later reaped as orphaned. The messages are mutually
inconsistent — one reports dropping the story and continuing, another reports
aborting for the same reason.

**Evidence — the baseline gate is defined as a pre-work check.** Its own failure
message states the contract: "configured gate failed on sprint merge base …
before any dev work started". At the time it ran, two stories had been working
for roughly 50 and 33 minutes.

**Ruled out — the gate timeout value being the defect.** The suite completes in
about 30s standalone on this host, well inside 120s. The timeout was exceeded
because of load the derivation does not account for, so raising it would mask
this instance without addressing why a pre-work check runs during work.

**Ruled out — the re-exec being wrong.** Reloading after the orchestrator's own
source changes is deliberate and necessary. The defect is that reloading is
implemented as a full restart of a procedure whose steps assume nothing is in
flight.

**Ruled out — duplicate of the config-contract issue already filed.** That issue
concerns a merged change invalidating the running sprint's configuration, which
is one way this startup path fails. This is the general form: the startup
sequence is re-executed against a live sprint, and any of its steps can
terminate the run. The two share a symptom and not a mechanism.

**Confirmed cause:** re-exec is implemented as re-entry into sprint startup
rather than as resumption of an in-flight run. Startup steps that are correct
exactly once — establishing a green baseline, reconciling worktrees, deriving
timeouts from expected load — are re-applied to a sprint whose stories are
already running, where their preconditions no longer hold.

**Fix-success criterion:** a sprint that re-execs mid-run resumes its in-flight
stories without re-running checks whose preconditions are limited to sprint
start, and without reclassifying its own live worktrees as foreign. Given this
run as input, the re-exec does not re-run the baseline gate, does not drop
`issue-1945`, and the sprint continues.

## Expected behavior

Reloading code mid-run is a continuation of the same run, and the work already
in flight is the state that continuation has to preserve. Implementing it as a
restart means every precondition established at launch is silently re-asserted
against a world that has moved on, and any one of them failing ends a sprint
that was otherwise healthy. A step that is only meaningful before work begins
belongs to starting, not to running, and the distinction has to survive the
process being replaced.

A run must also recognise its own work across that boundary. Live worktrees and
running agents belonging to the current sprint are not foreign state to be
reconciled, and treating them as such converts a routine reload into the loss of
whatever they contained. The consequence is not confined to the step that
misclassifies them, because subsequent cleanup then acts on that
misclassification as though it were established fact.

Finally, a derived limit is only valid under the conditions it was derived from.
A timeout computed from expected concurrency, applied when actual concurrency is
higher, is not a conservative estimate but a wrong one — and when exceeding it
is treated as evidence that the merge base is broken, the system reports a
conclusion about the code from a measurement that was really about its own load.

handoff.summary: Made mid-run re-exec a continuation rather than a re-entry into sprint startup. Added src/theforge/sprint/live_stories.py, which recognises the run's own in-flight stories across the os.execv boundary (pid survives exec, so an agent-group sidecar owned by this pid with a live pgid and a sandbox_dir under a story worktree identifies a story still executing). That live-slug set is threaded from the CLI into both the launch guard and run_sprint. The launch guard classifies those slugs REASON_IN_FLIGHT before any other reconciliation step, so they are neither re-dispatched (two agents in one worktree) nor dropped as active-worktree collisions, and their lock files survive the launch sweep (sweep_story_locks gained exclude_slugs, since execv releases the flock). sweep_orphan_worktrees gained protected_slugs because worktree liveness is not derivable from the git state it inspects. resolve_effective_gate_timeout gained an optional running_stories term (default 0 == today's math, appended-only diagnostic fields) so a continuation's derived timeout counts inherited agents. run_sprint skips the baseline gate when live agent groups are observed, recording the skip and its evidence in the sprint audit (baseline_check.skip_reason/skip_evidence) plus a baseline_gate_skipped structured log event; in-flight stories surface as PRESERVED and are excluded from preflight and dispatch.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A derived timeout is valid under the conditions it was derived from (gate timeout accounts for actual, not just expected, concurrency)
acceptance_criteria.notes: resolve_effective_gate_timeout(running_stories=N) makes demand = gate_cpu_cores * (max_parallel + running_stories); runner supplies len(live_story_slugs). Fresh-start behavior is bit-identical at the default 0. Covered by tests/test_sprint_gate_timeout_reexec_load.py (resolver + runner seam, both directions).

story_deviations: The plan's Step 1 allowed 'work already in flight' to include prior recorded outcomes. I restricted the baseline-gate skip to observed live agent process groups only: a sprint id is stable across separate invocations of the same sprint, so a recorded-outcomes signal would make an unrelated later run that happens to re-exec skip its baseline gate — losing the check instead of deferring it. Consequence: a re-exec landing in a gap between agent invocations still runs the gate (today's behavior, no regression).

Plan Step 3 left 'launchable/resumable' undecided; per the plan reviewer's P1 I chose exclude-from-re-dispatch-while-recorded-in-flight, since the original agent is still running in that worktree. The story is recorded PRESERVED (skipped bucket) rather than DROPPED (failed bucket), reusing an existing StoryOutcome instead of extending the enum.
Added src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py to the file set (flagged by the plan reviewer as missing from Step 3).
deferred_items: 7 tests fail in this sandbox for environmental reasons, unchanged by this work: 6 hit PermissionError creating POSIX semaphores (multiprocessing.Event) in test_sprint_lock.py / test_sprint_reexec_collision.py, and test_cut_rc_isolation.py hits 'mktemp: Operation not permitted'. Verified the same failures and causes are unrelated to these changes; the coordinator's gate runs outside this sandbox.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the P1: an in-flight story is no longer marked PRESERVED and abandoned — this process now waits for its inherited agent and resumes it. live_stories.py grew a lifecycle API (resolve_inherited_agents returning slug/pgid/sidecar, await_inherited_agents, reclaim_inherited_agents) with injectable liveness/kill seams. The launch guard no longer drops in-flight slugs at all: they are excluded from escalation scan, collision classification and lock sweeping, but stay schedulable and hold their launch lock, because no other process can adopt an agent group this pid owns. run_sprint builds _inflight_slugs and excludes them from startup triage, intake remediation and batch preflight (each reads or spends against a worktree being written right now), then dispatches them through the new _run_inherited_story: wait for the inherited group (bounded at half the story's worker timeout, interruptible by the stop event), reclaim/kill it if the wait overruns so two agents never share one worktree, triage the worktree at that point, and delegate to _run_single_story with resume semantics so the story re-enters review/dev/fresh and reaches a real terminal outcome. Inherited sidecars are unlinked once settled, so a later invocation's orphan reaper has nothing to act on. Live status annotates the story in-flight while it waits. Iteration-0 mechanics (baseline-gate skip on observed live agents with audited evidence, orphan-sweep protected_slugs, gate-timeout running_stories term) are unchanged.

story_deviations: Of the reviewer's two suggested remedies I took the first (wait, then re-enter the coordinator state machine). Teaching reap_orphan_agents to treat a REASON_IN_FLIGHT sidecar as resumable does not produce an outcome for the story — it only defers the loss to whichever later invocation decides to adopt it — whereas the spec's fix-success criterion requires the run to resume its in-flight stories.

The baseline-gate skip keys only off observed live agent process groups, not off prior recorded outcomes (which the plan also permitted): a sprint id is stable across separate invocations of the same sprint, so a recorded-outcomes signal would make an unrelated later run skip its baseline gate. A re-exec landing in a gap between agent invocations therefore still runs the gate — today's behavior, no regression.
Added src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py to the file set (flagged by the plan reviewer as missing from Step 3).

The coordinator's gate runs outside this sandbox.

If the sprint never reaches the in-flight story's dispatch (e.g. budget exhausted first), its inherited group is still left to the next invocation's reaper. That path is unchanged from before this work and is bounded by the same budget/skip semantics as any other story.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5] The change satisfies the mid-run re-exec continuation criteria; focused continuation and existing re-exec collision tests passed. | [google-gemini-3.5-flash] Successfully treated mid-run re-exec as a continuation of the sprint, skipping startup-only checks and preserving live worktrees. | [claude-sonnet] Gate-timeout/worktree-classification mechanics are correct and well-tested, but the in-flight story is abandoned rather than resumed: nothing re-enters its dev/review/merge pipeline, and the very next forge invocation's orphan reaper will kill its still-running agent process once this run's process exits, since the reaper keys off owner_pid being alive.

findings.description: When a re-exec detects a live in-flight story, run_sprint marks it StoryOutcome.PRESERVED and moves on without ever calling run_task (or any dev/review/merge phase) for that slug again in this process; the surviving dev-agent subprocess keeps running with no Python-level supervision, and once this sprint process exits, the next `forge sprint or forge status` invocation's reap_orphan_agents() sees the sidecar's owner_pid as dead and kills the still-running agent process group, discarding whatever work it had not yet committed.

finding_registry.description: When a re-exec detects a live in-flight story, run_sprint marks it StoryOutcome.PRESERVED and moves on without ever calling run_task (or any dev/review/merge phase) for that slug again in this process; the surviving dev-agent subprocess keeps running with no Python-level supervision, and once this sprint process exits, the next `forge sprint or forge status` invocation's reap_orphan_agents() sees the sidecar's owner_pid as dead and kills the still-running agent process group, discarding whatever work it had not yet committed.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Treat re-exec as continuation, not launch: preserve live sprint-owned work and skip startup-only validation once stories are already in flight. Thread explicit live-story state into launch guarding and audit/log the continuation decisions so operators can verify what was preserved or skipped.

steps.description: Separate sprint startup checks from re-exec continuation in the runner
steps.details: Use the existing reexec/reconcile path in run_sprint to gate startup-only work. Do not call _run_baseline_gate(config, resolved) during a mid-run re-exec continuation when work is already in flight; emit an explicit audit/display event that the baseline gate was skipped because the process is resuming an existing sprint generation. Keep normal fresh-start and explicit resume behavior unchanged unless the existing resume path already represents in-flight continuation.

steps.description: Identify current sprint-owned live stories before launch reconciliation
steps.details: At the point the re-exec path currently resolves prior outcomes, also derive the set of stories/worktrees that belong to the same sprint generation and still have live agent process groups or in-progress state. Pass that live-story identity into launch reconciliation alongside the existing prior_outcomes data, keeping the CLI layer thin and leaving ownership decisions in sprint/process modules.

steps.description: Classify own live worktrees as in-flight, not active-worktree collisions
steps.details: Extend acquire_launch_story_locks reconciliation so an active worktree whose slug is in the current sprint's live-story set is preserved and remains launchable/resumable instead of falling through to REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE. Ensure stale-worktree cleanup does not remove worktrees that were classified as current sprint-owned live work.

steps.description: Make adaptive gate-timeout accounting reflect actual re-exec load where a gate can still run
steps.details: Keep the existing resolve_effective_gate_timeout call path, but have runner supply actual live sprint load when resolving a timeout in any continuation path where a gate is still legitimately run. Preserve current fresh-start behavior based on configured --parallel, and include the actual-load value in the existing gate_timeout diagnostic output.

steps.description: Add integration coverage for mid-run re-exec continuation
steps.details: Add seam-level tests that simulate a re-exec with one completed/prior story and one still-running story with an active worktree/process record. Assert the baseline gate is not invoked, the live story is not dropped as REASON_ACTIVE_WORKTREE, stale cleanup does not remove its worktree, and the sprint continues scheduling remaining work.

steps.description: Add focused coverage for gate timeout load accounting
steps.details: Add or update resolver/runner tests to prove fresh-start timeout derivation remains based on configured parallelism while continuation-time derivation includes live running story load in the diagnostic inputs.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A sprint that re-execs mid-run resumes its in-flight stories without re-running checks whose preconditions are limited to sprint start.
Given this run as input, the re-exec does not re-run the baseline gate.
A sprint that re-execs mid-run resumes without reclassifying its own live worktrees as foreign.
Given this run as input, the re-exec does not drop issue-1945 and the sprint continues.
A derived gate timeout accounts for load from stories already running, not just configured --parallel, when applied during continuation.

risks.description: The exact durable source of truth for 'current sprint-owned live stories' may be split between state files and process-group records.
risks.mitigation: Prefer existing sprint generation state first and corroborate with process_group liveness; fail closed with an explicit operator-facing error if ownership cannot be established.

risks.description: Skipping too much launch reconciliation on re-exec could hide real foreign worktree collisions.
risks.mitigation: Only exempt worktrees positively identified as belonging to the same sprint generation; keep existing collision behavior for unknown slugs or mismatched generations.

risks.description: Resume and re-exec may currently share the same reconcile flag but have different intended semantics.
risks.mitigation: Audit existing resume behavior before changing shared branches, and add tests that preserve fresh-start and non-live resume behavior.
